data.body:
Pushed https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2328 (commit 782176dfdfe6). NOT submitted; awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

Scope correction found while implementing: the brief's premise that compose could certify was wrong. The REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH already in docker-compose.yml belongs to the opcert: service. The mcp: service mounts the key but never set the var either, so BOTH launch paths were key-less, not just blue-green. Fixed both, keeping compose the parity source of truth.

Mutation check: deleting the -e flag from mcp_run_new turns BOTH test_docker_run_points_the_container_at_the_opcert_key (new) and the pre-existing test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service RED. The second oracle exists only because the compose side was fixed too.

REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY: KEPT. It populates cfg.identity.signing_key for authorship signatures and is one of the two required inputs to mcp_server.compose_startup_opcert_binding (absent it the startup binding is skipped entirely). Removing it would have widened the bug.

Gates: make lint PASS, make typecheck PASS (682 files), test_module_size_contract 4 passed, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0, and 95 passed across test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py + test_mcp_on_box_infra.py + test_opcert_deploy_infra.py.

Related: closed ticket b173 (spoiled-bionic-goose) documented this exact seam and chose the ContextVar binding; this change adds the env fallback beside it rather than replacing it.
